plan.rationale: Small (440 LOC) but the hard decisions are architectural: how to shape a hand-written Vala binding over libghostty-vt's explicitly unstable C API, and how a status side-channel and a real terminal surface share one code path.

code.rationale: Raised two tiers: nearly all code here is hand-written FFI (vapi/libghostty-vt.vapi) where a wrong cname, ownership or out-param annotation compiles clean and corrupts memory at runtime — mistakes valac cannot catch and 440 LOC of tests barely constrain.

review.rationale: No CI, and the review target is binding correctness plus a socket that parses untrusted hook payloads — ownership/lifetime errors in the vapi are invisible to the existing asserts.

explore.rationale: 9 tracked files; finding things needs no reasoning, and the C headers in .local/include are the real reference material.

escalations.rationale: Hand-written FFI over an unstable API: ABI drift and ownership bugs are silent and memory-unsafe.

escalations.when: task touches src/main.vala socket or OSC parsing paths
escalations.rationale: Trust boundary: bytes arrive from hook scripts and are fed to a C parser.

escalations.when: tests fail twice in a row on the same task
escalations.rationale: Repeated failure signals the model has misread the API contract.

escalations.when: libghostty-vt is upgraded and osc-check or the build starts failing
escalations.rationale: Upstream renamed opaque handles (GhosttyOscParser to GhosttyOscParserImpl) once already; re-deriving a binding from changed headers is precise work.

notes: No CI and no type system covering the FFI boundary, so the usual 'strong safety net lets you drop a tier' logic is inverted here: the tests (tests/osc-check.vala, hooks/test-derive.sh) catch ABI drift but not lifetime or ownership errors. Re-calibrate if CI is added or if the project grows a large body of ordinary GTK UI code, which would justify dropping code to sonnet. fable was considered for plan and rejected: the repo is far too small, though a future full terminal-surface build-out on the render API would be the case for it.
